questions.q: What is a cross-cutting concern that AOP is designed to handle?
o: Logging, security checks or transactions applied across many classes
The main business rule of a single service
The schema of a single database table
The layout of one web page
questions.w: AOP lets you write such behaviour once and apply it to many methods without touching their code.

questions.q: How does Spring AOP apply advice to a bean?
o: It wraps the bean in a runtime proxy that runs advice around calls
It rewrites the bytecode of the class on disk
It copies the method body into every caller
It uses reflection to edit private fields
questions.w: Spring uses JDK dynamic proxies for interfaces and CGLIB subclass proxies otherwise. AspectJ weaving is a separate, heavier option.

questions.q: `OrderService.place()` calls `this.audit()`, which carries an `@Audited` aspect. Why is the aspect skipped?
o: The call on `this` bypasses the proxy, so the advice never runs
Aspects can only ever be applied to static methods
`@Audited` is ignored whenever it sits on a public method
Spring caches only the very first call of each method
questions.w: Self-invocation is the classic proxy pitfall. Move the method to another bean or inject the proxy.

questions.q: Which advice type runs whether the method returns normally or throws an exception?
o: `@After` (finally)
`@AfterReturning`
`@AfterThrowing`
`@Before`
questions.w: `@Around` is the most powerful: it controls whether and how the target runs, and can change the result.

questions.q: In an `@Around` advice, what happens if you never call `proceed()`?
o: The target method does not run
The target method runs anyway
Spring calls it after the advice finishes
An exception is thrown at startup
questions.w: That is how caching and security aspects short-circuit a call. Remember to return the value from `proceed()`.

o: An expression that selects which join points the advice applies to
The block of code that always runs before a method starts
A breakpoint that is set in the debugger by a developer
A configuration file that tells Spring how to build proxies
questions.w: Example: `execution(* com.bank.service..*.*(..))` matches every method in the service package.

questions.q: Which Spring features are implemented with AOP proxies?
o: `@Transactional`, `@Cacheable`, `@Async` and method security
`@Autowired` and `@Value`
`@Entity` and `@Id`
`@RequestMapping` and `@GetMapping`
questions.w: They all intercept method calls through a proxy, so they share the same limits: public methods, called through the bean reference.

questions.q: A `private` method is annotated `@Transactional`. What happens with Spring's proxy-based AOP?
o: The annotation has no effect, since proxies skip private calls
The transaction starts normally, just as the developer expected
The application fails to start with a configuration error
The method silently becomes public so the proxy can reach it
questions.w: Proxy-based AOP cannot intercept private methods or self-invocation. Use public methods on a separate bean.
